newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan rupee ends up in kerb, seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan rupee ends up in kerb, seen falling.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee ended 0.02 up at 41.33 to the dollar on Tuesday, but dealers said it would gradually weaken against the U.S. currency before the 1997/98 (July-June) budget to be announced on June 14.
"Today dollar supply matched demand, but the rupee might slip in the near term as there are fears of devaluation before the next budget," dealer Owais Kalia said.

The State (central) Bank of Pakistan rate, last changed on May 6, was 40.3300/40.5317 to the dollar. The premium on foreign exchange bearer certificates closed at 2.40 percent, up from Monday's close at 2.35 percent. -- Amir Zia 9221-5685192
